html:
Popeloutchom is the homeland of the Amah Mutsun, an Ohlone people of the Pajaro River valley and the coast around today's Santa Cruz and San Juan Bautista in central California. They spoke Mutsun, one of the Ohlone languages.

They lived by gathering acorns and seeds, fishing and hunting, and tended the land with fire. Between 1791 and 1797 the Spanish founded the missions of Santa Cruz and San Juan Bautista on their land and brought most Mutsun into them, where many died of disease; see Spanish missions in California. The Mutsun language survives on paper because a priest, Felipe Arroyo de la Cuesta, wrote down words and phrases in the early 1800s. The Amah Mutsun Tribal Band is working to revive it. Their neighbours to the south were the Salinan.
